title: Validation Runtime and Error Behavior
readerIntent: Understand how validation executes, reports failures, and remains observable.
owner: Owning validation services, pipelines, status definitions, and response handlers
summary: Validation is executed through declarative schema rules, services, interceptors, and pipelines, then normalized into stable status codes and safe diagnostic context.

sections.heading: Runtime behavior
items: Collect normalized input and resolved request context.
Run the applicable validators in deterministic order.
Accumulate field-level errors where safe and useful; stop immediately for security or invariant failures that must not continue.
Reject through the owning pipeline error path.
Resolve a registered stable status code and transport response.
Attach safe trace and layer context for diagnostics.

sections.heading: Error contract
items: Stable machine code for clients and monitoring.
Appropriate response classification without exposing internals.
User-facing messages supplied through the presentation/content contract where applicable.
Structured field or context details only when authorized and non-sensitive.
No credentials, secrets, password hashes, unrestricted records, or raw provider errors.

sections.heading: Operational signals
items: Failure rate by safe validation code, capability, route, and runtime context.
Repeated invalid attempts and authorization denials.
Import rejection counts and reconciliation outcomes.
Validator latency and downstream work avoided.
Configuration preview and activation validation failures.
